There is a common misconception about the difference between reinforcement and punishment. It is commonly thought that reinforcement is a pleasant response and punishment is an unpleasant response to a behavior. THIS IS INCORRECT!!

As you have already learned, reinforcement is something that increases a behavior. It may be pleasant or the removal of something unpleasant but in any case it increases a targeted behavior. �By contrast, punishment decreases a targeted behavior. Just like reinforcement, there is positive punishment (adding something. i.e. if you don't do your homework I will add more chores) and negative punishment (taking something away. e.x. if you don't do your homework you will not get to watch Netflix).�

In general, reinforcing desired behavior is more effective than punishing undesired behavior.�

  • A child is rewarded with a snack for good behavior (reinforce to increase good behavior)
  • a child is given a time out for bad behavior (Punish to decrease bad behavior)

Reinforcement does more to motivate good behavior in the future than the fear of punishment does to make the person avoid negative behavior. Therefore, reward is usually a more significant influence in shaping or changing one s behavior. Fear and anxiety generated by punishment usually hamper the learning process.�

  • Punishment stops undesirable behavior, but the behavior may reappear if the punishment ceases. Therefore, punishment is not a permanent solution for improving behavior.
  • Punishment may make a person or animal so fearful that they make even more mistakes than usual.
  • Punishment may lead to behavior that is less predictable than behavior that comes from rewarding desirable responses.
  • Punishment tells the individual what not to do; it does not indicate what the person should do.�

For example, suppose you are learning a new skill that you have never seen before.�You are handed a strange piece of equipment. You move your hand one way and you are punished.�You try another movement and are punished again.�You try a third way and receive more punishment. Have you learned the skill?�No! But you have probably picked up a great sense of fear.�
